# v0.6 offline restart verification

PR 5 of the [v0.6 plan](../PLAN.md#v06-draft-saved-runs-and-safe-resume)
extends the resume implementation merged in PR #69. The package version is
still `0.5.0`; these are checkout archive checks, not a published v0.6 release.
The separately authorized live pilot remains a release requirement.

## Enforcement coverage

`src/saved-runs/matrix.test.ts` exercises all six evaluator routes with both
worker selections: direct TypeSafe/Jev, Vercel/Jev, OpenRouter/Jev,
OpenRouter/OpenAI Decisions, and Cloudflare Clef/Clef-flash. Each of the 12
combinations has a successful three-segment task and an exhausted-budget task,
for 24 cases. Each segment binds a fresh evaluator using stored configuration
and reconstructed durable state. HTTP and coding-worker boundaries are
synthetic; Git inspection, policy, candidates, approval, execution transitions,
independent Node checks, snapshots, and the store remain real.

Successful tasks stop after implementation, resume to reread instructions and
stop again, then resume to reread and independently validate before explicit
completion acceptance. Seven distinct iteration reservations, one actual
worker dispatch, three trace segments, and fresh validation generation 3 are
asserted. A moderate completion assessment requires selecting FINISH and then
approving its resolved candidate. Previous approvals never execute again.

Exhaustion tasks consume both calls to the selected worker over separate
segments, retain the excluded worker restriction, and stop at the original
seven-iteration ceiling. Neither the model nor a manual alternative can grant
a third call, transfer allowances, or finish without validation. The terminal
result is `iteration_limit`, exit 1, with the patch and ledger preserved.

CLI failure checks block before evaluator binding, review, approval, or dispatch
for missing credentials, conflicting/empty selectors, changed Cloudflare
account, changed HEAD, unavailable repositories or instructions, run/worktree
owners, invalid snapshots, partial ledgers, and unresolved execution. Removed
validation scripts remain required after content review. Existing store and
loop fixtures additionally exercise partial writes, failed persistence at each
boundary, stale ownership, unknown schemas, cancellation, and explicit
evaluation recovery. These tests use deterministic fixtures without live calls.

## Process and terminal coverage

The [optional harness](../scripts/terminal/README.md) retains the 33 original
unsaved terminal scenarios and adds 14 saved-run scenarios, for 47 per full
matrix. Each worker uses three separate CLI processes for its accepted task;
additional processes stop at the continuation review with typed stop, EOF,
Ctrl+C, and timeout. Styled Codex enables networking explicitly; plain Claude
retains restricted tools. Empty/invalid review input grants nothing. Declined
reviews leave checkpoint and ledger bytes unchanged and release ownership.

Each walkthrough also checks six preflight blockers per worker in bounded pipe
processes, plus credential-free list/show. After the second clean stop, the
harness changes instruction and check contents. The final review displays
these changes, rereads instructions, performs independent validation, and
requires a separate completion approval. Actual worker launch counts, durable
iterations, validation generations, trace linkage, and empty ownership
directories are asserted. State homes are isolated outside worker repositories
on each platform; real operator history and credentials are never loaded.

Existing assertions retain parameter visibility, wrapping, terminal injection
and credential redaction, raw mode/cursor/signal cleanup, POSIX terminal flags,
prompt and active-process interruption, partial edits, current-generation
validation, and conventional exits. Both decision-only JSON/trace cases retain
schema 1; orchestration traces retain schema 2. There are no runtime dependency,
permission, policy, or package-version changes in this milestone.

## Evidence and limits

Local results and the checkout archive receipt are retained outside Git under
`/home/peterc/.cache/dev-v06-verification/20261023`. Native Windows fixtures,
reports, and installed consumer are under
`C:/Users/pcruc/AppData/Local/Temp/dev-v06-20261023`. Failed and intermediate
captures remain alongside the final results.

The candidate archive contains 86 files and no source, tests, terminal driver,
or native harness dependencies. Its SHA-256 is
`0260aa55faf6c724a79b27b75b38c221b232242addaab71ae3c7329c7667715a`;

## v0.6 draft: saved runs and safe resume

Originally drafted on 2026-10-17. Refined on 2026-10-22 after publication of
v0.5.0 and merge of its publication record in
[PR #64](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/pull/64). PR 1's storage
contract merged in [PR #66](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/pull/66)
at `d102eec`. PR 2's loop integration merged in
[PR #67](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/pull/67) at `4be904c`.
Local history merged in [PR #68](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/pull/68)
at `7ac6cd9`. Explicit resume merged in PR #69 at `88312e2`, followed by
restart/platform verification in PR #70 at `1801d78`. The v0.6 scope is approved
for implementation. The live pilot and release are the current milestone;
this work remains unpublished until the v0.6 release.

**Release outcome:** an operator can stop an opted-in task, close the terminal,
inspect its history, and continue it in a new CLI process without losing its
approved context or resetting its limits. Partial edits stay in the worktree.
Resuming requires fresh repository checks, validation, and action approvals.

### Product scope

| Priority | Deliverable | Observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required | Opt-in saved orchestration | The CLI prints a run ID, checkpoints progress, and explains whether the stopped run can continue. |
| Required | Local history and detail | The operator can see the task, repository, status, consumed/remaining budgets, pending checks, and any resume blocker without credentials or network access. |
| Required | Explicit continuation | A cleanly stopped run continues in a new process on the same machine and canonical Git worktree, starting at its next unused iteration. |
| Required | Conservative failure handling | Storage errors, unresolved execution, incompatible records, and concurrent ownership stop execution with a specific explanation. |
| Required | Verified release | Offline restart/failure coverage, installed-package terminal checks, and a recorded live stop/resume pilot pass before publication. |

Keep this release focused. Cross-machine transfer, crash recovery for uncertain
execution, background runs, worker-native conversation restoration, automatic
retries/failover, expanded permissions/budgets, a dashboard, and new providers
are outside v0.6. Run deletion, export/import, and automatic retention cleanup
are also deferred; the first version documents storage and manual housekeeping
for inactive records. Existing runs without saving remain supported.

The [v0.5 routing limitation](docs/presentation/v0.5-routing-mitigation-results.md)
remains visible: invalid distributions are rejected at the same `0.001`
tolerance, and explicit recovery consumes the remaining iteration budget.
Persistence must retain that failure and recovery requirement across restarts.
An upstream provider correction is separate work; this release does not claim
to improve the model's probability output.

### Operator workflow

Proposed command contract, to be frozen in the first implementation PR:

```text
dev-agent . "Fix the bug and add regression tests" --orchestrate --save-run
dev-agent --list-runs
dev-agent --show-run <run-id>
dev-agent --resume <run-id> [--plain]
```

Saving is opt-in and requires `--orchestrate`. The supported saved-run target
is a Git worktree with a resolvable HEAD; ordinary unsaved operation keeps its
existing repository support. The initial review explains what is stored and
where. Stop, EOF, and signals retain their existing meaning and exit behavior;
the terminal summary also prints the run ID and continuation status.

Listing and showing are bounded, read-only local operations. A missing
repository or missing provider credential must not prevent inspection. Plain
output remains available; history JSON output is deferred so existing
decision-only `--json` behavior stays stable. Run IDs resolve only within the
application store and never accept arbitrary file paths.

Resume uses the stored task and repository rather than new positional
arguments. It shows the prior stop, remaining limits, refreshed repository
changes, pending checks, and immutable selections before the operator chooses
to continue or stop. That review grants no action approval. Resume rejects
task, worker, network, mock/live, or provider/model overrides; presentation
choice may change. Recovery from an evaluation failure remains explicit and
does not get counted or requested twice by overlapping resume/recovery prompts.

Example: three consumed evaluations and one Codex call leave five iterations
and one Codex call. Resume starts at iteration four. Fresh validation consumes
those remaining iterations; finishing is never promised when too little
budget remains. Finished and exhausted runs stay inspectable.

| Last condition | Proposed continuation behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Typed stop or EOF, with durable state and completed cleanup | Eligible after repository/configuration review. |
| Evaluation failure stopped by the operator | Eligible with explicit recovery and budget remaining. |
| SIGINT/SIGTERM, including during a worker, with recorded outcome and completed cleanup | Eligible after refresh; partial edits and charged attempts remain. |
| Abrupt exit, unresolved attempt/owner, or incomplete required write | Blocked; show the last trustworthy evidence and uncertainty. |
| Finished or iteration limit reached | Inspection only; resume cannot extend the run. |
| Unknown schema, altered/stale record, wrong worktree, changed HEAD, or unverifiable identity | Blocked; never repair the record or relocate the task implicitly. |

### State and durability requirements

Use a dedicated versioned saved-run format, separate from diagnostic JSONL
traces. The current traces deliberately truncate data; they cannot supply
resume state. Parse saved records as untrusted input. Integrity checks do not
turn stored repository or issue text into authoritative instructions. The
first contract must classify each saved field:

| Treatment | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Restore after strict validation | Original task; bounded approved clarification/issue context and provenance; failure history; consumed budgets and original ceiling; immutable provider/model, mock/live, worker selection, and network permission. |
| Refresh or revalidate | Canonical repository/Git worktree identity and HEAD; working-tree changes; instruction fingerprints; validation scripts, coverage, and all original required checks. |
| Retain only as history | Earlier test outcomes, worker summaries, proposals/approval receipts, interruptions, and segment metrics. |
| Never persist | Credentials, raw environment values, transport instances, AbortSignal, raw rejected provider responses, or an executable approved candidate. |

Required context must fit the schema without lossy truncation of acceptance
criteria or validation requirements. Apply bounded, credential-aware text
handling; if required context cannot be represented safely, stop the saved run and
explain the blocker instead of silently making a resumable record. Opt-in
storage can contain task text and source excerpts; document that local data
and its retention without claiming encryption or perfect secret detection.

The store belongs to the operator and must be outside worker-writable
repositories. PR 1 must settle platform paths, restricted access, link/path
rejection, explicit byte/event/record limits, atomic replacement, flush/write
ordering, and schema compatibility. A checksum alone cannot make a checkpoint
authoritative. Bind it to an integrity-checked, sequenced local attempt ledger
and reject mismatched or older records. No schema migration or trace import is
required for v0.6; incompatible records remain non-executable.

State the trust boundary honestly: protecting records from repository text,
restricted workers, corruption, and checkpoint-only rollback does not establish
protection from a compromised operator account or rollback of the entire local
store. The contract must explain which authority is protected and prove the
claimed behavior on POSIX and Windows before persistence enters the loop.

Consume an iteration durably before evaluation. After a fresh action approval,
record the dispatch boundary before every tool/worker execution and reserve a
worker allowance before starting that worker. Commit outcomes without charging
twice. An uncertain reservation stays charged and blocks continuation; never
invent an approval or replay an uncertain action. Required persistence or trace
write failure stops further evaluation/execution and drains active cleanup.

Acquire exclusive run ownership and a canonical-worktree lock. Every
app-managed orchestration invocation, including an unsaved one, must participate
in the same ownership protocol so the order of startup cannot bypass the lock.
Coordination metadata does not opt an unsaved run into task persistence. A
stale/unresolved owner blocks execution; a saved PID alone cannot authorize lock
removal or process killing. External editors and older CLI versions do not
participate in this protocol; repository refresh must still detect drift.
Mark a stop resumable only after the action outcome, repository refresh, process
cleanup, and final durable transition are known.

Freeze non-secret configuration identity and reload credentials from the
operator's environment. Explicit provider/model or Cloudflare account changes
block continuation. The present configuration has no non-secret account ID for
the other providers; PR 1 must decide and document credential-continuity rules
before enabling resume. A variable name cannot prove account identity, and
credential values must not be stored to fill that gap. Preserve the selected
model identifier; a provider alias such as `jev-latest` does not guarantee the
same underlying served version on a later day.

### Continuation and policy requirements

Reinspect the same canonical worktree and unchanged HEAD. Compare bounded
working-tree fingerprints, including untracked changes relevant to the task;
status filenames alone do not prove unchanged contents. Show drift for review,
invalidate stale reads, and require new approved reads for changed instruction
files. An unavailable or ambiguous comparison blocks continuation. Never reset
Git, restore files, discard partial edits, or attribute operator edits to a
worker. Retain exact linked-issue identity and clarification provenance; any
new issue fetch still uses the existing approved read boundary.

Start a fresh validation generation on resume. Keep original required checks,
including those named by the task, issue, and clarifications; a removed script
cannot silently remove its requirement. Prior passing checks and worker claims
cannot establish completion. A prior failure cannot establish current-generation
repair eligibility: rerun the relevant independent check before another repair
when policy requires it. Rebuild every candidate from current state and obtain
a new action approval, including acceptance review for `FINISH`.

The original eight-iteration maximum, two calls per adapter, 95% automatic
completion threshold, preparation gates, repeated-failure rules, and fixed
worker/network selection span every process segment. Preserve a lower original
iteration ceiling if one was used. Never reset or transfer budgets, redirect an
excluded route, relax probability validation, or silently switch providers.

Link each segment's traces and summaries to the saved-run ID. Preserve trace
compatibility and keep reporting metrics outside AgentState and authorization.
Use a fresh local monotonic clock per segment; time between processes is neither
active work nor prompt wait. Show cumulative attempt counts from durable records
without double-counting recovery rows or treating metrics as permission.

### Six proposed implementation PRs

Each PR has a reviewable result and focused tests. Add the contract and failure
fixtures before wiring saved data into execution; use the current small typed
modules rather than introducing a workflow framework.

1. [x] **Saved-run contract and storage foundation.** Define schema version 1,
   field bounds, lifecycle/stop reasons, ledger ordering, repository identity,
   configuration/credential continuity, integrity, and ownership. Implement the
   bounded store and offline fixtures without an executable resume route.
   Demonstrate clean read/write, malformed/incompatible input rejection,
   altered counters/permissions, stale snapshots, partial writes, and lock
   contention. Record POSIX/Windows guarantees and limits. Delivered in the
   [saved-run v1 storage contract](docs/saved-runs-v1.md), with 17 focused
   tests. POSIX permissions, file flushes, atomic checkpoint replacement,
   rejected partial writes, event/checkpoint integrity, stale approvals, and
   lock ownership are covered. Windows inherits parent ACLs and skips directory
   flush; native Windows verification remains in PR 5. Provider/model identity
   is frozen, Cloudflare account identity is fingerprinted, and other provider
   credential continuity is explicitly unverifiable; resume must disclose that
   and require an operator decision. No CLI or executable resume route is part
   of this PR.
2. [x] **Opt-in saving throughout the loop.** Add `--save-run`, create the run
   before its first evaluation, and persist reservations and outcomes at the
   established boundaries. Integrate worktree ownership for saved and unsaved
   runs. Preserve signal cleanup, prompts, trace writes, unsaved task behavior,
   and existing exit codes; document ownership conflicts. Print the saved ID/status.
   Inject failures before and after evaluation, approval, dispatch, outcome,
   and clean stop; assert no unrecorded execution, double charge, or false
   resumable status. Delivered in PR #67, with 1,439 tests passing locally
   alongside type checking and build.
3. [x] **Local run history.** Add `--list-runs` and `--show-run` with bounded
   listing and a way to inspect an older known ID. Display status, task/repo,
   budgets, selections, pending validation, last failure, and precise blockers.
   Cover empty/corrupt stores, unavailable repositories, terminal sanitization,
   and plain/styled output. Prove these commands work without credentials,
   provider calls, worker launches, or repository mutations. The implementation
   lists up to 20 records (unreadable first, then recent updates), supports any
   known ID directly, and shows the last 12 events in detail. Inspection does
   not initialize storage or acquire locks; repository/configuration preflight
   is implemented in PR 4. Delivered in PR #68, with all 1,481 tests passing
   serially alongside type checking, build, and a compiled CLI smoke.
4. [x] **Explicit resume.** Add CLI compatibility checks, exclusive ownership,
   preflight/review, fresh evaluator binding, repository/context refresh,
   validation invalidation, and entry at the next unused iteration. Add a
   two-process happy path for each worker selection and explicit recovery
   continuation. Prove old approvals never execute, budgets span restarts, and
   all current policy/candidate/final-approval guards still apply. The current
   implementation adds a bounded content sidecar tied to the clean-stop ledger,
   refuses older stops without it, rechecks content after the operator review,
   and requires fresh instruction reads and independent validation. Linux
   subprocess fixtures cover both worker selections. Delivered in PR #69, with
   all 1,513 tests passing serially alongside type checking, build, and a
   compiled CLI smoke. The full provider/platform matrix and installed-package
   verification remain in PR 5.
5. [x] **Restart and platform verification.** Extend deterministic integration
   coverage across all six supported evaluation routes and both workers.
   Exercise repeated restarts, exhausted budgets, missing/conflicting config,
   changed HEAD/worktree/content/instructions/scripts, concurrent owners,
   storage errors, EOF, signals, and unresolved execution. Extend the compiled
   and installed PTY/Windows ConPTY matrix on supported Node versions. Keep
   existing decision-only, unsaved orchestration, and JSON behavior covered.
   The [offline verification record](docs/saved-runs-verification.md) documents
   the three-segment provider/worker matrix, preflight failure checks, and
   compiled/installed terminal evidence. Delivered in PR #70, with 1,551 tests,
   local compiled/installed matrices, and all six Ubuntu/Windows Node 22/24/26
   CI jobs passing. The live pilot remains separate.
6. [ ] **Live pilot and v0.6.0 release.** Freeze a candidate archive and bounded
   protocol, obtain operator authorization for live calls, then run the pilot
   below before any publication. Fix failures in a separately identified
   candidate with retained observations. Record package/source provenance,
   migration/storage guidance, limitations, and release acceptance. Give
   advance npm authentication notice before timed login/publication; verify
   the published archive and a fresh registry installation afterward.
   Preparation uses the [bounded live pilot protocol](docs/workflows/v0.6-live-protocol.md).
   Preparing the candidate and fixtures does not authorize live calls or publication.
   The first authorized candidate failed its required Codex scenario after
   passing fresh validation but exhausting eight iterations before acceptance.
   Preserve its [results](docs/workflows/v0.6-live-results.md). Resume context
   and task-file read preferences are corrected offline; the
   [retest amendment](docs/workflows/v0.6-live-retest-amendment.md) requires
   separate collection authorization. The separately approved
   [2026-10-28 retest](docs/workflows/v0.6-live-retest-results-20261028.md)
   completed Codex stop/resume, but Claude reached `iteration_limit` after an
   evaluation recovery despite a valid patch and fresh validation. Four
   launches, sixteen evaluations, and two worker attempts are retained; the
   active-interruption slots were not launched. Worker-token reporting added
   afterward has offline evidence only. The live release gate remains blocked.
   A follow-up adds optional explicit task acceptance alongside a clear
   file-read route after a worker attempt and fresh passing validation. The
   read remains the default; acceptance still requires selecting `FINISH`
   and approving its resolved candidate. The
   [offline correction record](docs/workflows/v0.6-completion-review-fix.md)
   retains the live failure and describes its deterministic reproduction.
   Further live collection requires a frozen amendment and authorization.

### Verification and release acceptance

The live pilot is a release requirement, planned from the outset. It uses the
exact installed candidate, actual default TypeSafe/Jev evaluation, and actual
workers with separate action approvals. Freeze tasks, fixtures, stop points,
maximum launches/time/spend, acceptance oracles, and candidate/tool versions
before calls. Planning this pilot does not authorize spending or publication.

| Required live scenario | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Codex task stopped after implementation, then resumed in a new process | Same run/task, preserved patch and consumed call, fresh independent validation, and explicit accepted completion within the original limits. |
| Claude task stopped after implementation, then resumed in a new process | The same evidence, using the other presentation mode and unchanged restricted-worker tools. |
| Clean signal interruption of an active worker, then continuation | Observed partial work, process-tree cleanup, charged attempt, recorded interruption, fresh validation, and a valid next approved action. Freeze the selected worker and fixture before launch. |

Use deterministic fault injection for repeated malformed evaluations, storage
failures, and exact crash windows; label that evidence separately from live
observations. Retain every live provider failure, routing detour, exhausted run,
and protocol deviation. No replacement runs or hidden budget increases; new
collection requires a recorded amendment. Natural invalid responses keep their
explicit recovery gate. A small successful pilot establishes the exercised
workflow, not a statistical routing-reliability or performance claim.

- [ ] Storage, ownership, configuration identity, and attempt-ordering decisions
  are documented and proven by focused failure tests; no contract questions
  remain that could authorize duplicate execution or reset a budget.
- [ ] Clean stops resume in a new process for both workers. Exhausted, finished,
  uncertain, incompatible, tampered, and concurrently owned runs cannot execute.
  Partial edits and original acceptance/validation requirements survive.
- [ ] Fresh current-generation validation and separate task acceptance are
  enforced after resume, including through manual alternatives and repair.
- [ ] History, plain/styled prompts, signals/EOF, traces, secret exclusion, and
  metrics pass their regressions. Earlier diagnostic traces remain diagnostic.
- [ ] Focused tests, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and
  `pnpm env:check:schema` pass. Fresh installed-package checks and POSIX/Windows
  terminal matrices pass against the release candidate.
- [ ] The live scenarios have recorded outcomes and the operator has accepted
  any remaining limitations before publication. If a required scenario fails,
  fix and reverify it or explicitly revise scope; offline tests alone cannot
  silently substitute for the live gate.
- [ ] README/help, changelog, storage/compatibility instructions, release
  evidence, archive checksums, npm/GitHub publication, and independent registry
  installation verification are complete.

### State and durability requirements

Use a dedicated versioned saved-run format, separate from diagnostic JSONL
traces. The current traces deliberately truncate data; they cannot supply
resume state. Parse saved records as untrusted input. Integrity checks do not
turn stored repository or issue text into authoritative instructions. The
first contract must classify each saved field:

| Treatment | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Restore after strict validation | Original task; bounded approved clarification/issue context and provenance; failure history; consumed budgets and original ceiling; immutable provider/model, mock/live, worker selection, and network permission. |
| Refresh or revalidate | Canonical repository/Git worktree identity and HEAD; working-tree changes; instruction fingerprints; validation scripts, coverage, and all original required checks. |
| Retain only as history | Earlier test outcomes, worker summaries, proposals/approval receipts, interruptions, and segment metrics. |
| Never persist | Credentials, raw environment values, transport instances, AbortSignal, raw rejected provider responses, or an executable approved candidate. |

Required context must fit the schema without lossy truncation of acceptance
criteria or validation requirements. Apply bounded, credential-aware text
handling; if required context cannot be represented safely, stop the saved run and
explain the blocker instead of silently making a resumable record. Opt-in
storage can contain task text and source excerpts; document that local data
and its retention without claiming encryption or perfect secret detection.

The store belongs to the operator and must be outside worker-writable
repositories. PR 1 must settle platform paths, restricted access, link/path
rejection, explicit byte/event/record limits, atomic replacement, flush/write
ordering, and schema compatibility. A checksum alone cannot make a checkpoint
authoritative. Bind it to an integrity-checked, sequenced local attempt ledger
and reject mismatched or older records. No schema migration or trace import is
required for v0.6; incompatible records remain non-executable.

State the trust boundary honestly: protecting records from repository text,
restricted workers, corruption, and checkpoint-only rollback does not establish
protection from a compromised operator account or rollback of the entire local
store. The contract must explain which authority is protected and prove the
claimed behavior on POSIX and Windows before persistence enters the loop.

Consume an iteration durably before evaluation. After a fresh action approval,
record the dispatch boundary before every tool/worker execution and reserve a
worker allowance before starting that worker. Commit outcomes without charging
twice. An uncertain reservation stays charged and blocks continuation; never
invent an approval or replay an uncertain action. Required persistence or trace
write failure stops further evaluation/execution and drains active cleanup.

Acquire exclusive run ownership and a canonical-worktree lock. Every
app-managed orchestration invocation, including an unsaved one, must participate
in the same ownership protocol so the order of startup cannot bypass the lock.
Coordination metadata does not opt an unsaved run into task persistence. A
stale/unresolved owner blocks execution; a saved PID alone cannot authorize lock
removal or process killing. External editors and older CLI versions do not
participate in this protocol; repository refresh must still detect drift.
Mark a stop resumable only after the action outcome, repository refresh, process
cleanup, and final durable transition are known.

Freeze non-secret configuration identity and reload credentials from the
operator's environment. Explicit provider/model or Cloudflare account changes
block continuation. The present configuration has no non-secret account ID for
the other providers; PR 1 must decide and document credential-continuity rules
before enabling resume. A variable name cannot prove account identity, and
credential values must not be stored to fill that gap. Preserve the selected
model identifier; a provider alias such as `jev-latest` does not guarantee the
same underlying served version on a later day.

### Continuation and policy requirements

entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
                 (positional, --checkpoint, or --commit) and a checkpoint that
                 has been pushed. A commit SHA is resolved to its checkpoint
                 by that repo's Entire API, so prefixes cannot be used here.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied,
                   including its subagent task records under "tasks".
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --task           With --transcript, stream a subagent's stored transcript
                   instead, selected by tool_use_id or agent_id (as listed
                   under "tasks" in --json).
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint. This is the only
                part of this command that writes: it stores the summary on the
                checkpoint and spends tokens with the configured summary
                provider. Every other mode only reads.
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

When to use this:
Reading a checkpoint is free: with no flags, or with --json, --full,
--transcript or --raw-transcript, this only reads and is safe to run
whenever you need the context. --generate is the exception — it writes a
summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider,
so pass it only when the user asked for a summary. To see what subagents
did, read "tasks" in --json, then stream one subagent's transcript with
--transcript --task <tool_use_id>.

Current repo: gh/petercr/jev-orchestrator  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string             Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                 Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force                         Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full                          Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate                      Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
      --insecure-http-auth            Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json                          Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                     Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager                      Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript                Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                   Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (gh/owner/name, et/project/repo, entire://<host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>, or entire://<host>/et/<project>/<repo>), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all                    Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int             Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short                         Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int   Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.
      --task string                   Subagent task (tool_use_id or agent_id) whose stored transcript --transcript streams
      --transcript                    Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout (a session's, or a subagent's with --task)

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import unicodedata
from urllib.parse import unquote

root = Path.cwd()
plan = root / 'PLAN.md'
text = plan.read_text()
anchors = set(re.findall(r'<a\s+id="([^"]+)"', text))
counts = {}
in_fence = False
for line in text.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('```'):
        in_fence = not in_fence
    if in_fence:
        continue
    match = re.match(r'^#{1,6}\s+(.+?)\s*#*$', line)
    if not match:
        continue
    heading = match.group(1).lower()
    slug = ''.join(c for c in heading if c in ' -_' or unicodedata.category(c)[0] in 'LN')
    slug = slug.replace(' ', '-')
    count = counts.get(slug, 0)
    counts[slug] = count + 1
    anchors.add(slug if not count else f'{slug}-{count}')

checked = 0
errors = []
for name in subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '*.md'], text=True).splitlines():
    document = root / name
    for target in re.findall(r'\]\(([^\s)]+)\)', document.read_text()):
        path, marker, fragment = target.partition('#')
        if '://' in path:
            continue
        destination = (document.parent / unquote(path)).resolve() if path else document.resolve()
        if destination != plan:
            continue
        if marker and unquote(fragment) not in anchors:
            errors.append(f'{name}: missing plan anchor {fragment}')
        checked += 1

for document in (plan, root / 'README.md'):
    for target in re.findall(r'\]\(([^\s)]+)\)', document.read_text()):
        path = target.split('#', 1)[0]
        if path and '://' not in path and not (document.parent / unquote(path)).exists():
            errors.append(f'{document.name}: missing local target {path}')

legacy = {'proposed-release-sequence', 'v04-draft-reliable-task-workflows', 'v05-candidate-terminal-presentation-and-interaction', 'v06-draft-saved-runs-and-safe-resume'}
assert legacy <= anchors, 'Legacy roadmap anchors must remain available'
v06 = text.split('## v0.6 release: saved runs and safe resume', 1)[1].split('## v0.3.0 release:', 1)[0]
assert '[ ]' not in v06, 'Completed v0.6 gates must be checked'
assert 'No v0.7 scope or release date has been selected.' in text
if errors:
    raise SystemExit('\n'.join(errors))
print(f'Passed: {checked} roadmap links, local targets in PLAN/README, four legacy anchors, and completed v0.6 checklist.')
